units.title: Problem Solving & Web Development (HTML)
units.essentialQuestion: How does the structure of a webpage reflect the logic of how computers communicate?
units.description: Students transition from Scratch to text-based coding, learning HTML to build structured web pages. They connect prior knowledge of algorithms to web development.

lessons.title: Problem Solving Review & Computational Thinking
lessons.objective: Apply decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithmic thinking to solve problems.

lessons.title: HTML Introduction & Structure
lessons.objective: Explain the structure of an HTML document using tags, elements, and the DOM hierarchy.

lessons.title: HTML Content Elements
lessons.objective: Create web pages using headings, paragraphs, lists, links, and images.

lessons.title: HTML Web Page Project
lessons.objective: Design and build a multi-page website on a topic of choice using semantic HTML.

units.title: Interactive Programming with Game Lab (Part 1)
units.essentialQuestion: How do coordinates, shapes, and variables create the building blocks of interactive programs?
units.description: Students transition from HTML to interactive programming in Code.org's Game Lab, learning drawing, variables, random numbers, sprites, and text.

lessons.title: Plotting Shapes & Drawing in Game Lab
lessons.objective: Use coordinates and shape functions to draw geometric compositions on the Game Lab canvas.

lessons.title: Shapes and Parameters
lessons.objective: Explain how parameters modify function behavior and adjust shape properties through experimentation.

lessons.title: Variables & Random Numbers
lessons.objective: Implement variables and random number generation to create dynamic, non-repetitive program outputs.

lessons.title: Mini-Project: Robot Faces
lessons.objective: Create a program that generates unique robot face compositions using variables and randomization.

lessons.title: Sprites & Sprite Properties
lessons.objective: Create and manipulate sprite objects, modifying properties like position, size, rotation, and visibility.

lessons.title: Text & Mini-Project: Captioned Scenes
lessons.objective: Integrate text display with sprite compositions to create captioned digital scenes that tell a story.

lessons.title: Draw Loop & Sprite Movement
lessons.objective: Explain the draw loop concept and implement continuous sprite movement using velocity and position updates.

units.title: Interactive Programming with Game Lab (Part 2)
units.essentialQuestion: How do conditionals and user input transform a program into a truly interactive experience?
units.description: Students advance to conditionals, user input handling, collision detection, and complex sprite movement, building toward full interactive applications.

lessons.title: Mini-Project: Animation
lessons.objective: Create a sprite-based animation using the draw loop, costume changes, and timed sequences.

lessons.title: Conditionals & Keyboard Input
lessons.objective: Implement conditional statements that respond to keyboard input to control sprite behavior.

lessons.title: Mouse Input & Interactive Card
lessons.objective: Design an interactive greeting card that responds to both mouse and keyboard events using conditional logic.

lessons.title: Velocity & Collision Detection
lessons.objective: Implement velocity-based movement and collision detection between sprites to create realistic interactions.

lessons.title: Mini-Project: Side Scroller
lessons.objective: Build a side-scrolling game incorporating sprite movement, collision detection, and scoring.

lessons.title: Complex Sprite Movement & Collisions
lessons.objective: Implement advanced movement patterns including acceleration, deceleration, and multi-object collision handling.

lessons.title: Mini-Project: Flyer Game
lessons.objective: Design and develop a top-down flyer game integrating all Game Lab skills: sprites, conditionals, collisions, and scoring.

units.title: Game Design Project (Semester 1 Capstone)
units.essentialQuestion: What separates a game that's technically functional from one that's genuinely fun?
units.description: Students apply the full game design process to plan, develop, playtest, refine, and present an original game in Game Lab.

lessons.title: Functions Introduction
lessons.objective: Define functions and explain how they promote code organization and reusability.

lessons.title: Game Design Process Introduction
lessons.objective: Describe the stages of the game design process and develop a comprehensive game design document.

lessons.title: Project Game Design – Development Sprint
lessons.objective: Independently develop a complete game in Game Lab applying functions, conditionals, collisions, and variables through iterative development.

lessons.title: Peer Review & Revision
lessons.objective: Conduct structured peer reviews using established criteria and implement revisions based on feedback.

lessons.title: Game Share Lab & Voting
lessons.objective: Present completed games, articulate design decisions, and evaluate peer games using criteria-based assessment.

units.title: Data Representation & Information Systems
units.essentialQuestion: How does a computer see the world — and what gets lost in translation?
units.description: Students explore how computers represent and process information through binary, ASCII, images, and numbers.

lessons.title: Semester Reflection & Representation Matters
lessons.objective: Evaluate Semester 1 growth and explain why digital representation systems matter in computing.

lessons.title: Patterns and Representation
lessons.objective: Identify patterns in data and explain how patterns enable efficient representation of information.

lessons.title: ASCII and Binary Representation
lessons.objective: Convert between binary, decimal, and ASCII to demonstrate how computers encode text and numbers.

lessons.title: Representing Images
lessons.objective: Explain how digital images are represented using pixels and binary data, and create a pixel art composition.

lessons.title: Representing Numbers & Combining Representations
lessons.objective: Analyze how different data types are combined in computing systems and explain overflow/precision limitations.

lessons.title: Keeping Data Secret
lessons.objective: Describe basic encryption concepts and demonstrate a simple cipher to encode and decode messages.

lessons.title: Create a Representation
lessons.objective: Design an original representation system for a specific type of information and justify design choices.

lessons.title: Problem Solving with Data & Structuring Data
lessons.objective: Organize raw data into structured formats and use data to solve a defined problem.

lessons.title: Interpreting Data
lessons.objective: Interpret data visualizations to draw evidence-based conclusions and identify potential biases.

units.title: Data, AI & Machine Learning
units.essentialQuestion: When a machine learns from data, who is responsible for what it decides?
units.description: Students explore how data drives decisions, learn about automation and machine learning concepts, and complete a recommendation system project.

lessons.title: Making Decisions with Data
lessons.objective: Analyze a dataset to make an evidence-based decision and explain their reasoning.

lessons.title: Automating Data Decisions
lessons.objective: Explain how algorithms automate decision-making processes and identify advantages and limitations.

lessons.title: Problem Solving with Big Data
lessons.objective: Describe how large datasets are used to identify trends and solve complex problems across industries.

lessons.title: Data and Machine Learning
lessons.objective: Explain how machine learning systems use training data to make predictions and classifications.

lessons.title: Make a Recommendation Project
lessons.objective: Design and develop a data-driven recommendation system that collects, analyzes, and presents personalized suggestions.

lessons.title: AI & Machine Learning – Ethical Considerations
lessons.objective: Evaluate the ethical implications of AI and machine learning, including bias, privacy, and societal impact.

units.title: Electricity, Circuits & Physical Computing
units.essentialQuestion: What happens when code meets the physical world — and a light actually turns on?
units.description: Students transition to physical computing, learning electrical fundamentals, circuit design, Ohm's Law, and Arduino programming.

lessons.title: Introduction to Electricity & What is a Circuit?
lessons.objective: Define voltage, current, and resistance and explain how a closed circuit allows electricity to flow.

lessons.title: Ohm's Law & PhET Simulation
lessons.objective: Apply Ohm's Law (V=IR) to calculate voltage, current, and resistance using the PhET circuit simulator.

lessons.title: Circuit Research & Circuit Lab
lessons.objective: Research circuit types (series/parallel) and construct physical circuits to verify theoretical predictions.

lessons.title: Voltage Relationships & Ohm's Law Quiz
lessons.objective: Analyze voltage relationships in series and parallel circuits and demonstrate mastery of Ohm's Law.

lessons.title: Arduino Research & LED/Breadboard Introduction
lessons.objective: Research Arduino microcontrollers, identify hardware components, and construct basic LED circuits on a breadboard.

lessons.title: Paper Circuit Project
lessons.objective: Design and build a paper circuit that demonstrates understanding of circuit fundamentals.

lessons.title: Intro to Arduino Programming & Blink Projects
lessons.objective: Write Arduino code to control LED blinking patterns, applying programming concepts to physical hardware.

lessons.title: Micro Servo & Big Servo
lessons.objective: Program servo motors to specific angles using Arduino, demonstrating control of mechanical output through code.

lessons.title: Photoresistor & Arduino Quiz
lessons.objective: Implement a photoresistor sensor to create a light-reactive system and demonstrate understanding of sensor input.

lessons.title: TinkerCAD Circuit Simulations (RGB LED, Light Show)
lessons.objective: Design and simulate advanced Arduino circuits in TinkerCAD, programming RGB LEDs and multi-component systems.

units.title: 3D Design & Shark Tank Capstone
units.essentialQuestion: How do you turn a problem you care about into a product someone would actually buy?
units.description: Students learn 3D modeling in TinkerCAD and apply it to an entrepreneurial Shark Tank project — designing products, calculating costs, surveying markets, and pitching to judges.

lessons.title: TinkerCAD 3D Design Introduction
lessons.objective: Navigate the TinkerCAD 3D workspace and create basic 3D models using primitive shapes and grouping.

lessons.title: Pobble 3D Design Project
lessons.objective: Design a 3D character model applying advanced TinkerCAD techniques including alignment, holes, and custom shapes.

lessons.title: Shark Tank Introduction & Planning
lessons.objective: Identify a problem worth solving and develop an initial product concept using the design thinking process.

lessons.title: Target Market Research
lessons.objective: Research and define target market using demographic data and consumer analysis techniques.

lessons.title: Benefits, Features & Production Costs
lessons.objective: Differentiate product features from benefits and calculate production costs to determine pricing strategy.

lessons.title: Market Survey
lessons.objective: Design and conduct a market survey, then analyze results to validate product-market fit.

lessons.title: Presentation Slides & Website Creation
lessons.objective: Create a professional pitch deck and product website that communicate value proposition to potential investors.

lessons.title: 3D Product Prototype Design
lessons.objective: Design a 3D-printable product prototype in TinkerCAD that demonstrates the product concept.

lessons.title: Shark Tank Prototypes & Refinement
lessons.objective: Develop, test, and refine physical and digital prototypes through iterative design cycles.

lessons.title: Shark Tank Presentations
lessons.objective: Deliver a persuasive product pitch to a panel of judges, defending design, market research, and business model.

lessons.title: TinkerCAD Dreamhouse Project
lessons.objective: Design a detailed 3D architectural model in TinkerCAD applying advanced modeling techniques and spatial reasoning.
